questions.stem: According to the passage, how do the roots of trees help the soil?
options: They take oxygen out of the soil.
They make the soil dry and hard.
They turn the soil into desert.
They bind the soil and hold it in place so that rain cannot wash it away.
questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.passage: Trees are among the most useful of nature's gifts to human beings. They give us shade in the hot summer months, and their falling leaves enrich the soil in which they grow. From trees we obtain timber for our houses and furniture, fruit for our tables, and firewood for our kitchens. But the value of trees goes far beyond these everyday uses. Their roots bind the soil and hold it firmly in place, so that heavy rain cannot wash it away. Their leaves take in the carbon dioxide that we breathe out and give back the oxygen without which no living creature could survive. Forests also attract rain and keep the air cool and clean. Yet, despite knowing all this, people continue to cut down trees carelessly to make room for houses, roads and factories. When too many trees are cut, the rain washes away the fertile topsoil, rivers overflow, and once-green land slowly turns into desert. It is high time we understood that planting a tree is not a small act of charity but a duty we owe to those who will come after us.

questions.stem: What mistaken belief about students does the author mention?
options: That students should play all day.
That the only duty of a student is to study and pass examinations.
That students should never read books.
That games are more important than studies.
questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.passage: Games and sports have an important place in the life of a student. Many people think that the only duty of a student is to study his books and pass his examinations. This is a mistake. A student who spends all his time bent over his books, and never steps out into the playground, may do well in his examinations, but he often grows weak in body and dull in mind. Games keep the body fit and the mind fresh. A short game in the evening drives away the tiredness of a long day's study and sends the student back to his books with new energy. But the benefits of games are not limited to health alone. On the playing field a student learns lessons that no classroom can teach him. He learns to obey the captain, to play fair, to keep his temper when he loses, and to work with others for the good of his team. These are the very qualities that he will need in later life, when the playground of childhood has given way to the harder field of the world. A good player, it is often said, makes a good citizen.

questions.stem: Why does the author call a good book 'a faithful friend'?
options: Because books can quarrel with us.
Because a book never tires of us, never quarrels, and keeps us company when we are lonely.
questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.passage: The habit of reading is one of the greatest pleasures that a person can enjoy, and also one of the most useful. A good book is a faithful friend. It never grows tired of us, never quarrels with us, and is always ready to keep us company when we are lonely. Through books we can travel to distant lands without leaving our chairs, and meet the wisest men and women of every age, though they died hundreds of years ago. A person who has learned to love reading is never quite alone and never quite without resources. He can turn to a book for knowledge when he is puzzled, for comfort when he is sad, and for entertainment when he is bored. But like every good habit, the love of reading must be formed early and formed with care. Those who read nothing but cheap and worthless books gain little from the hours they spend, for the mind takes the shape of what it feeds upon. To choose one's books wisely is, therefore, almost as important as to read them at all.

questions.passage: Time is one of the most valuable things we (79)________. Once a moment has passed, it can never be (80)________ again, no matter how rich or powerful we may be. Many people, however, do not (81)________ the value of time until it is too late. They waste their precious hours in idle gossip and useless amusements, and then (82)________ that the day is over before their work is done. A wise person, on the other hand, makes the (83)________ of every hour. He knows that success in life (84)________ largely on the proper use of time. He does his work at the (85)________ time and never puts off till tomorrow what he can do today. Such a person is (86)________ respected by all, for he can be depended (87)________ in every situation. If we wish to make our lives useful and happy, we must therefore learn to (88)________ our time with the greatest care.
